passage:
Counsellor's note, Class 9.
Avni came to my room with her friend Kashish, who had noticed Avni hiding her phone screen. Avni said a stranger online had been telling her she was "so mature, not like the others", and that their chats must stay secret because people wouldn't understand. She had felt special at first, then uneasy when messages arrived late at night.
I told her that flattery plus secrecy is a warning sign, that she had done nothing wrong, and that none of this was her fault. I thanked Kashish for staying beside her. With Avni's agreement we called her parents in, saved the messages and blocked the contact.
I will follow up with Avni next week.

qa.q: What did the stranger say about their chats?
qa.a: The stranger said the chats must stay secret because people wouldn't understand.

qa.q: How did Avni feel about the stranger's attention, and how did that change?
qa.a: She felt special at first, then uneasy when the messages arrived late at night.

qa.q: What did the counsellor do that protected Avni?
qa.a: The counsellor told her it was not her fault, brought in her parents with her agreement, saved the messages and blocked the contact.

qa.q: How might Kashish have felt about noticing and speaking up?
qa.a: Kashish was probably worried and unsure, yet stayed beside Avni, and being thanked by the counsellor would show that speaking up was right. 🤍

grounding: Shows a teen receiving flattery and requests for secrecy from an online stranger, and a counsellor naming the warning signs and involving parents.

passage:
Ishita was fourteen and lived above her father's hardware shop in Sagar. Since the summer holidays, someone called "Rohan_travels" had been messaging her on the photo app. He said her pictures were beautiful. He said she was "so mature, not like other girls your age."

At first it made her glow. Then, on Tuesday night, he wrote: "Don't tell your parents about me. They'll never understand what we have. This is our secret."

Ishita stared at the screen. Her stomach went cold. Something about the word "secret" felt wrong.

The next morning, her elder brother Amandeep, home from college, found her sitting on the stairs, pale. "What's wrong?"

She showed him the chat, hands shaking. "I didn't do anything bad, I swear."

"I know you didn't. This isn't your fault." Amandeep took her straight down to the shop. Their father read every message, then blocked the account with her, took screenshots and called the cybercrime helpline before lunch. "You were brave to show us," he said.

qa.q: What did the stranger ask Ishita to keep secret?
qa.a: He asked her not to tell her parents about him and to keep it "our secret."

qa.q: What was Ishita feeling when she read the word secret?
qa.a: Ishita felt a cold, frightened unease, sensing that something was wrong.

qa.q: Why was showing Amandeep and her father the right move?
qa.a: It ended the secrecy and brought in trusted adults, who blocked the account, saved screenshots and called the helpline that same day.

qa.q: How did Ishita's father respond, and why did it matter?
qa.a: He acted calmly and quickly and told her she was brave, which showed her she was not to blame.

grounding: It shows a teen targeted by an online stranger's flattery and requests for secrecy, recognising the grooming warning signs and telling trusted adults, who make clear it is not her fault.

passage:
In Manchester, Nadia had been playing an online game for months. One player, "Skyfall22," always teamed up with her. He said she was the best player he'd met, "way more mature than most people your age." He started sending private messages.

On Saturday he wrote, "You're special, Nadia. But let's keep our chats just between us, okay? Parents don't get this stuff." Then he asked which school she went to.

Nadia felt a strange knot in her chest. She liked the praise. But the secret, and the school question, made her uneasy.

On Monday she told her friend Chidi at lunch. Chidi frowned. "That's exactly what they warned us about in the assembly. Secrets plus compliments."

"But what if I'm overreacting?"

"Then your dad will say so. Tell him today."

That evening, Nadia showed her dad the messages. He read them quietly, then hugged her. "You did everything right. None of this is your fault." They blocked the player, saved the chats and reported the account to the game and the police online that night.

qa.q: What did Skyfall22 ask Nadia after telling her to keep chats secret?
qa.a: He asked which school she went to.

qa.q: What was Nadia feeling after the Saturday message?
qa.a: Nadia felt a knot of unease, liking the praise but disturbed by the secret and the school question.

qa.q: What warning signs did Chidi point out?
qa.a: Chidi pointed out that secrets plus compliments are warning signs of grooming, as they had been told in assembly.

qa.q: How did Nadia's dad respond, and why was it important?
qa.a: He hugged her, said it was not her fault, and blocked, saved and reported the account that night, so she was protected and not blamed.

grounding: It shows a teen flattered by an online stranger who asks for secrecy, recognising the grooming warning signs and telling a trusted adult who acts the same day.
